title: Introduce service keystore mirroring and jurisdictional audit retention hook
author: Amina Patel
description: Context: Customers operating under strict jurisdictional constraints requested an option to maintain verifiable key usage proofs in a second jurisdiction without transferring primary key custody. This PR implements a lightweight keystore mirroring sidecar and a jurisdictional audit retention hook that annotates and enforces retention metadata on audit records. Motivation: provide a compliant read-only proof path for KMS usage and make audit retention configurable per-jurisdiction without changing customer primary CMK ownership. High level changes: - Add keystore mirror sidecar (pkg/kms/mirror) that mirrors key usage events and metadata (not raw key material) to a configurable shadow keystore endpoint; the sidecar ensures only provenance proofs are copied and signs a mirror-proof envelope. - Add audit retention middleware (api/audit/retention_middleware.go) which attaches jurisdiction and retention-profile labels to audit writes and enforces immutable retention windows for records marked as jurisdiction-bound. - Installer hooks and Helm templates to opt in the keystore mirror for Private deployments (helm/charts/private/templates/keystore-sidecar.yaml, cmd/installer/hooks/jurisdictional_retention.go). - Docs and runbook: docs/compliance/keystore-mirroring.md describing design, threat model, and compliance considerations. - Proto+API: proto/kms/mirror.proto and small additions to the KMS service API to accept mirror proof envelopes. - Tests: tests/integration/kms_mirror_test.go and unit tests for retention enforcement. Single-line commit summary: 1) add mirror sidecar scaffold and wire to KMS client; 2) implement mirror envelope signer and persistence; 3) audit retention middleware and installer hook; 4) helm/values and docs; 5) integration tests and CI fixes. Files changed (high-level): - pkg/kms/mirror/sidecar.go (new) - pkg/kms/mirror/envelope_signer.go (new) - api/audit/retention_middleware.go (new) - cmd/installer/hooks/jurisdictional_retention.go (new) - helm/charts/private/templates/keystore-sidecar.yaml (modified) - proto/kms/mirror.proto (new) - tests/integration/kms_mirror_test.go (new) Behavioral notes and compatibility: - The sidecar mirrors only metadata and signed usage proofs; no secret key material leaves the primary keystore. - Default behavior is opt-in via installer flag --enable-keystore-mirror; hosted customers are not affected unless explicitly enabled by support. - During mirror target downtime the sidecar buffers envelopes to local durable queue (size-limited) and exposes per-tenant metrics for dropped envelopes. Rollout plan: 1) merge behind feature flag and add to Private installer docs; 2) deploy to internal canary region with retention enforcement disabled for three days; 3) enable retention enforcement in a staged multi-tenant rollout (10% -> 50% -> 100%) with telemetry gates. Security review highlights: - Mirror envelopes are HMAC-signed using a per-instance signing key stored in the instance keystore; verification is implemented on the mirror reader to prevent replay. - Audit retention middleware enforces only retention metadata on audit entries and rejects deletion requests that overlap retention windows. - Added unit tests for signature verification and retention edge cases. Testing and CI: - Unit suite: complete. - Integration: new integration tests simulate mirror downtime and retention-enforced deletion attempts. - Security scanning: dependency and SCA scans run and green. Migration notes: - Existing audit records are not retroactively modified; a small migration tool (scripts/migrate/add_retention_tags.sh) is included to tag prior records for customers who opt in post-migration. - Operators must provision mirror target endpoints and set retention profiles in the installer values prior to enabling the enforcement flag. Risks and mitigation: - Risk: mirror queue growth under sustained target outage. Mitigation: circuit-breaker configured to drop oldest envelopes after configurable threshold and emit alert. - Risk: accidental enabling for hosted customers. Mitigation: default to off and require support-approved tenant flag for Hosted. Related: ENG-8854 (product request), SUP-2102 (support runbook).
review_conversation: Liam Chen (reviewer): Can we expose metrics for queued / dropped envelopes and a per-tenant telemetry tag? Amina: Added tenant-level metrics (mirror.queue_size, mirror.dropped) and included them in release notes.

Sofia Ramirez (reviewer): How does this interact with key rotation? Specifically, will mirror verification break across rotations? Amina: Mirror envelopes are signed with an instance-level signing key independent of customer CMKs; we added a rotation handler that keeps a verification window and publishes rotation events to metrics.

Ethan Blake (reviewer): Please confirm the retention middleware does not change audit storage format. Amina: Confirmed — middleware annotates entries with retention metadata fields (namespace:retention_profile) and enforces deletion checks; storage schema unchanged, annotations are optional fields.
Sofia Ramirez: Request that we run a canary with retention enforcement disabled first. Amina: Canary plan added to rollout and runbook with gating checks in Console.
Liam Chen: Minor nits on naming and log levels for sidecar; addressed in second commit.
Ethan Blake: Approve after tests and docs updated. (approval)
release_notes:
- New optional keystore mirroring sidecar that copies signed usage proofs (no key material) to a jurisdictional shadow keystore endpoint.
- Jurisdictional audit retention middleware that tags audit entries with jurisdiction and retention-profile and enforces immutable retention windows when enabled.
- Opt-in via Private installer flag --enable-keystore-mirror and helm values.
- Added new observability metrics: mirror.queue_size, mirror.dropped, audit.retention_rejects.
testing_instructions: Run unit tests: make test/unit. Run integration: make test/integration TEST_ARGS=--mirror-target=local. Installer: set values.keystoreMirror.enabled=true and values.keystoreMirror.target=... then run ./installer apply --dry-run to validate. To simulate retention enforcement: POST /audit/delete with an entry falling inside a retention window and assert 403.
notes_for_ops: Ensure mirror target endpoint is provisioned and access-controlled. Configure retention profiles before flipping enforcement flag. Watch mirror.queue_size and mirror.dropped; retention_rejects will surface deletion attempts that overlap immutable windows.
